  executing. Actions Claude identifies as safe are
  executed, while actions Claude identifies as risky
  are blocked and Claude may try a different
  approach. Ideal for long-running tasks. Sessions
  are slightly more expensive. Claude can make
  mistakes that allow harmful commands to run, it's
  recommended to only use in isolated environments.
  Shift+Tab to change mode.

❯ Run this command: python3 -c "print(1)"

⏺ Running the check command
  ⎿  $ python3 -c "print(1)"

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Auto mode can't check actions in this session

  Auto mode's safety check runs on the server. Your
  requests go through 127.0.0.1:51184, and the check isn't
  getting through.

  You can stay in auto mode and approve each action that
  needs the check yourself.

  Or you can leave for accept edits mode, which has no
  safety check, and auto mode stays off. These then run
  without asking: file edits and commands such as rm and
  mv in your working folders, some tools, such as
  subagents and scheduled tasks, and anything allowed by
  rules that auto mode set aside, such as Bash(*). This
  turn stops, so its waiting actions don't run, but
  background tasks go on. Claude goes on at your next
  message, or sooner.

  To get the check back, ask whoever runs your gateway to
  pass it through: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permiss
  ion-modes#server-side-classifier-review

  Enter to stay in auto mode · shift+Tab to leave for
  accept edits mode and stop · Esc to cancel
